items.question: Does memory help Brian finish real work after a restart or compaction?
items.why: This is the primary goal, and R2 showed that recall questions still do not test it.
items.next_step: R17: Claude designs saved-feedback work comparison, then Corvid independent review; no trial released.
items.current_answer: Two operational paired pilots completed; both arms succeeded in each. General benefit unestablished; no first-pass timing estimate established.
items.for_brian_why: We still don’t know whether memory helps your real work. Answering that matters more than improving another lab score.
items.for_brian_next: We will test whether remembering your preferences helps produce usable scripts and instructions. The study design comes first.

items.question: Can we trust the checks used to judge memory?
items.why: A work-task comparison is only useful if its checks are sound; local gate failures establish that risk, and the new reports add unverified leads.
items.next_step: No successor released. Tern reviews new evidence only at 2026-09-26T17:15:00Z against WORK-BENEFIT-DIRECTION-DISPOSITION.json; no automatic task search.
items.current_answer: R15: selected unit check accepts conforming drains and rejects tested substantive mistakes; integration coverage absent, provenance limits recorded.
items.for_brian_why: We could choose the wrong memory tool if its test gives misleading grades. Our own checks have failed before.
items.for_brian_next: The audit is finished. Another check audit waits until there is a justified new experiment.

items.question: Can memory accept real updates without losing facts that are still true?
items.why: The tested protection worsened false replacement; new supersession and dedup reports suggest relevant cases, but not a validated replacement.
items.next_step: Compare reported authority/supersession/dedup cases to existing fixtures before any tier1 selection.
items.current_answer: Tested key-equality protection failed on its observed shape; no general mechanism verdict.
items.for_brian_why: Memory needs to learn what changed without losing facts that are still true. The protection we tested made that problem worse.
items.for_brian_next: I’ll check whether the reported update failures add anything to the cases we already tested.

items.question: When does missing or crowded-out evidence cause mistakes in real work?
items.why: Delivery loss is observed, but task harm is not; choose the real task before expanding retrieval benchmarks.
items.next_step: Keep accumulation/benchmark ideas as candidates, not substitutes for work-task outcomes.
items.current_answer: Local delivery loss observed; link to task harm unestablished.
items.for_brian_why: Useful evidence sometimes gets crowded out. We haven’t shown when that causes mistakes in your work.
items.for_brian_next: Once we have a real task, I’ll check whether missing evidence changes how well it gets done.

items.question: What does the September 20 evidence establish?
items.why: R1 answered this bounded synthesis question; the overall work-benefit question remains open.
items.next_step: Revisit only if newly admitted evidence changes the synthesis.
items.current_answer: R1 accepted retrospective synthesis with recorded provenance normalization.
items.for_brian_why: We reviewed the old results. They still don’t show memory helping your real work.
items.for_brian_next: I’ll revisit this summary when we have new evidence worth adding.
